title: Quality and Interaction Analytics
blurb: Evaluation forms, two average-score formulas, categories, and sentiment windows.

lessons.title: Forms, plans, and no retention rule
lessons.summary: Quality Management builds forms and plans, then can lead to coaching. The welcome page says there is no defined rule for how long evaluations must be kept.

p: The Quality Management welcome page says you build evaluation forms and plans, distribute interactions for evaluation, and may then design coaching. Some screens show evaluations inside a time frame. The page says there are no defined rules for how long evaluations must be retained.

Pages such as Quality Performance, Forms, Scorecard, and Quality Plan need at least View on Teams and on Groups. Without those permissions, the parts of the page that use Teams and Groups data are restricted. The permission names include Teams view, edit, create, and deactivate, and Groups view, edit, create, and delete.

sections.h: Advanced, Premium, and the default formula
p: QM Advanced adds category analysis for voice and text interactions. Defining categories is only for QM Advanced. QM Premium adds behavior performance indicators for interactions. The page says prebuilt reports and QM dashboard widgets use the Average of values formula by default.
The score-metric permission is Quality Management (CXone) Tools > Average Quality Score Configuration, view or edit. The next lesson does the arithmetic.

lessons.title: 70 percent is not 73.3333
lessons.summary: The welcome page walks Sanity QA through both formulas. Averaging the percentages gives 70. Averaging the points gives 73.3333. The page's Vijay figures do not match each other.
objectives: Know which formula the widgets use

p: The welcome page's percentage table gives Sanity QA 3 ÷ 5 × 100 = 60% and 8 ÷ 10 × 100 = 80%. The later walkthrough adds 60 and 80 to get 140, divides by 2 evaluations, and gets 70%.
That is one agent. The page also shows a team rollup. This lesson stops at the agent so the two formulas stay comparable.

For the same Sanity QA pair, points earned are 3 + 8 = 11 and points possible are 5 + 10 = 15. The page prints 11 / 15 × 100 = 73.3333. Prebuilt reports and QM dashboard widgets use this average-of-values formula by default.
The percentage table lists Vijay at 100% and 30%. A later percentage walkthrough lists Vijay at 70% and 60%. Those pairs do not match. This lab does not pick a Vijay score.

steps.detail: The page prints 73.3333.

lessons.title: A form is questions, then an activation
lessons.summary: Forms can be standard, self-assessments, or collaborative. A draft cannot be used. A critical answer can fail the whole evaluation. The supervisor review window on the form settings is 30 days.
objectives: Keep IA Category as a header field

p: Form Manager says a form is a collection of questions used to evaluate interactions. Forms can be standard evaluations, self-assessments by the agent, or collaborative evaluations by the evaluator and the agent. You can score questions, make the form change with the answers, and mark a critical question. A critical answer can fail the entire evaluation. The page's example is a greeting question where No fails the form.

Create the form in Quality Management under Manage Forms. You still have to activate it. Statuses are Draft, Active, and Inactive. Save & Activate is the live path. Save as Draft stays a draft. Rename is only for a draft. Up to five custom headers can be added.

The header catalog includes Agent Sentiment, Customer Sentiment, Enlighten Sentiment, IA Category, and QM Category. Those are fields the form can show. This page does not say every tenant has Interaction Analytics turned on.

If Send to Supervisor is selected, the supervisor must finish the review within 30 days, and then the rest of the flow continues. N/A on a scored question is left out of the score. Saving an active form without updating the version is only for cosmetic edits. Non-cosmetic fields are grayed out while that option is on.

lessons.title: Categories, up to 2,000
lessons.summary: Interaction Analytics categories are groups of transcript data. The system supports up to 2,000. Workspace edits wait until you click Update Data. A deleted category does not come back.
objectives: Separate the workspace from the Categories page

p: The Categories page says categories are the foundation of Interaction Analytics. They are data groups used to parse transcripts. Rules and filters make trends easier to see. Category sets group related categories. Out-of-the-box examples named on the page include Intent to Buy and Risk Aversion. Templates named for import include Agent Performance, Intent to Buy, Sentiment, and Contact Center Highlights.

Workspaces are for review. From a workspace you can filter, see widgets, and save the current filters as a category. The Categories page is where you import, merge, split, move, delete, and edit rules. Matching interactions show the tags that caused the match, such as keywords or sentiment.

If the company has Interaction Analytics in more than one language, pick a language before category work on the Language Model page. The system supports up to 2,000 categories. Edits you make for workspaces do not apply until you click Update Data. You can queue another reprocess if you click it again while one is running. Unsaved changes turn the group icons orange.

You can undo rule edits. Discarding unsaved changes cannot be undone. Deleting a category or a group cannot be undone, and deleting a folder deletes what is inside it. Sample interactions let you see the effect before you apply a set. Editing an imported template does not change the original template.

lessons.title: Beginning, end, and three seconds of silence
lessons.summary: Overall sentiment is the whole interaction. Beginning sentiment is the first 400 words or the first 30 percent, whichever comes first. End sentiment is the last 30 percent. Mixed is not available on the beginning or the end. Notable silence is three seconds or more.
objectives: Keep frustration separate from negative sentiment

p: The Improve Sentiment page says you can filter a workspace by Positive, Negative, Neutral, or Mixed sentiment, and by when it occurred. Overall is the whole interaction. Beginning sentiment uses the first 400 words or the first 30 percent, whichever occurs first. End sentiment uses the last 30 percent. Mixed is not available for beginning sentiment or for end sentiment.

The recommended workspace adds two Overview Bars, Top Categories, Silence Percentage, two Sentiment Trends, Frustration Trend, Top Company Profile Terms, and two Metrics widgets. Metrics can show 1 to 25 teams or skills. The default number to show is 10. One Overview Bar and one Sentiment Trend stay on the client. The other pair is switched to the agent.

sections.h: Silence, frustration, and the Classics story
p: Silence is notable at three seconds or more. Total notable silence is the sum of those periods. The page says chat and digital tend to show a higher silence percentage than voice because the gaps between replies vary. Frustration is not the same thing as negative sentiment. Frustration is measured for the client.

The page's Classics story says the Emerald City team's interactions averaged 20 percent higher sentiment than the Kansas team, and that a later Analytics Metric Statistics report showed the Kansas team had improved positive sentiment by 7 percent. Those figures are the story on the page, not a benchmark for another contact center.

lessons.title: JSON every 400 records, and closed tickets
lessons.summary: Interaction Analytics can export JSON every 400 records or every 6 minutes, whichever comes first. The data page names four prebuilt reports. Closed or resolved CRM tickets can be searched for evaluation.
objectives: Keep ticket evaluation on resolved or closed

p: The data and reporting page says Interaction Analytics can export to a secure external bucket. Each export can include internal, contact, and agent metadata, annotations such as sentiment and frustration, categories, transcripts, and CXone metrics if you have Interaction Analytics Premium and at least one CXone use case.

The files are JSON. A file is written every 400 records or every 6 minutes, whichever comes first. New and reprocessed records are interleaved. Duplicates can appear inside a file and across files. Order is not guaranteed.

The same page names four prebuilt reports: Analytics Metric Statistics, Analytics Category Statistic s, Analytics Metric Comparison, and Analytics Metric Trend. The second name is printed with a space before the final s. This lab does not rename it. A short training video is mentioned for the metric and category statistics reports. This campus does not host that video.

The QM welcome page says Quality Management for CRM Ticketing puts a ticket on Ticket Search once it is resolved or closed. You can see the interactions and the agent and system comments. The page points at Evaluating a Ticket, Calibrating an Evaluation of a Ticket, MyZone for QM Ticket Evaluators, and Quality Planner for Tickets. Those four procedure pages were not opened for this lesson, so their steps are not repeated here.
